tests: driver formulas (risk reduction: (ARO before - ARO after) x loss per event); PARTIAL: cyber-insurance saving added outside the engine

source.title: The Total Economic Impact of ThreatLocker Cybersecurity Solutions
source.how_opened: page HTML fetched with curl and text-extracted; table 'Reduced Risk Of Data Breach' (Ref A1-A8, At, Atr)
source.caveat: Forrester Total Economic Impact study, commissioned by the vendor (vendor-favourable by design)

mapping_notes: Forrester uses the annual likelihood of one or more breaches (68%) as the expected number of events per year. Strictly that is a probability, not a Poisson rate; the engine treats ARO the same way, so the arithmetic matches.

aro_before = 68% x 81% (breaches from internal or external attack on the organization) = 0.5508. A 99% reduction gives aro_after = 0.5508 x 1% = 0.005508. Loss per event = $3,010,000 mean cumulative cost of breaches (Forrester research).

PARTIAL: the printed benefit also includes a cyber-insurance saving of $2,800,000 x 10% = $280,000 per year, which is not a risk-reduction driver. The test adds 280,000 x (1 - 15%) outside the engine.
Published A5 is $1,641,329; exact arithmetic gives $1,641,328.92 (difference under $1).

inputs.published_as: constant effect in all three years
A1 68% likelihood x A2 81% addressable (Forrester security survey 2024)
A3 99% reduction, from vendor customers' interviews
A4 mean cumulative cost of breaches (Forrester research)
